title: Construct Unified Registry
description: Single source of truth for teams, specialists, roles, contracts, and policies. Consolidates what was previously split across five separate files: teams.json, teams-registry.json, registry.json, contracts.json, and role-manifests.json.

version.description: Schema version. Version 2 is the unified registry.

teams.description: Map of team id -> team definition. Teams are the primary organizational unit with explicit decision rights, escalation paths, and charter.

specialists.description: Map of specialist id (e.g., cx-engineer) -> specialist definition. Every specialist declares exactly one team.

contracts.description: Map of contract id -> contract definition. Contracts are producer→consumer handoffs with preconditions, postconditions, and schemas.

policies.description: Map of policy id -> policy definition. Policies enforce team decision rights, approval requirements, and governance gates.

team.description: Organizational team with explicit owner, decision rights, forbidden decisions, escalation path, and charter.

id.description: Unique team identifier (e.g., product-group, engineering-group, quality-group).

owner.description: Role id of the team owner/lead. Must be a role that has at least one specialist assigned.

roles.description: List of role ids that constitute this team.

decisionRights.description: Decisions this team is authorized to make (e.g., intake-triage, design-approval, deployment, scope-change).

forbiddenDecisions.description: Decisions this team explicitly cannot make. Attempts escalate automatically.

escalationPath.description: Chain of escalation for unresolved decisions. First element is the team owner role, then higher-level escalations.

charter.description: One-paragraph mission statement: what this team owns, what it doesn't own, and key constraints.

owner.description: Direct contact for the team owner.

evidence.description: Primary sources justifying this team's structure (interviews, job specs, ADRs, organizational research).

specialist.description: An AI specialist (cx-* agent) with skills, fence, model tier, and event watchers.

name.description: Specialist id without cx- prefix (e.g., engineer, qa, architect). Combined with prefix to create cx-engineer, cx-qa, etc.

displayName.description: Human-readable specialist name (e.g., Engineer, Quality Assurance, Architect).

description.description: Short description of what this specialist does.

team.description: Team id this specialist belongs to. Every specialist declares exactly one team.

role.description: Role within the team: owner (team lead), member (regular), or temporary.

modelTier.description: Which model tier to use for this specialist: standard or reasoning.

reasoningEffort.description: Effort level for extended thinking (if using reasoning model).

skills.description: List of skill paths this specialist has (e.g., docs/prd-workflow, architecture/api-design).

events.description: Trigger events that activate this specialist (e.g., test.fail, handoff.received, pr.opened).

fence.description: Access control fence for this specialist.

allowedPaths.description: Paths/glob patterns this specialist can read/write.

allowedCommands.description: Commands this specialist can execute (bash, bd, git, etc.).

allowedBdLabels.description: Beads labels this specialist can use when creating/updating issues.

approvalRequired.description: Actions requiring approval before execution (e.g., commit, push, edit:lib/**).

docArtifacts.description: Doc artifact types this specialist can author (e.g., prd, adr, memo, incident-report).

watchConditions.description: Conditions that should trigger proactive engagement (e.g., high-ambiguity-deep-work, flaky-tests, stale-alignment-census).

prompt.description: Optional prompt configuration overrides for this specialist.

customInstructions.description: Custom instructions appended to the base prompt.

contract.description: Service contract between producer and consumer specialists. Defines inputs, outputs, preconditions, postconditions, and team boundaries.

producer.description: Specialist id or role that produces the output (e.g., cx-researcher, user, construct).

consumer.description: Specialist id or role that consumes the output (e.g., cx-architect, cx-product-manager, construct).

mustContain.description: Fields that must be present in the input.
Fields that must be present in the output.

schema.description: Path to JSON Schema for the output.

preconditions.description: Conditions that must be true before this contract executes.

postconditions.description: Conditions that must be true after this contract completes.

teamBoundary.description: Whether this handoff crosses a team boundary and what approval is needed.

crosses.description: Whether this contract crosses a team boundary.

requiresApprovalFrom.description: Team ids that must approve this cross-team handoff.

policy.description: Governance policy enforcing team decision rights, approval requirements, and gates.

id.description: Unique policy identifier (e.g., release-gates, security-approval, design-approval).

owner.description: Team id that owns and enforces this policy.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this policy enforces.

enforcement.description: hard = blocks execution, soft = warns but allows.

mode.description: How this policy is enforced: approval (must approve), veto (can block), audit (log only), escalation (route upward).

requiresApprovalFrom.description: Team ids that must approve before execution.

mayVetoFrom.description: Team ids that can veto this decision.

escalatesTo.description: Team ids to escalate to if blocked or disputed.

decisionRights.description: Decisions this policy governs (e.g., deployment, scope-change, security-approval).

conditions.description: Conditions under which this policy applies.

evidence.description: References to source documents or decisions justifying this policy.

allOf.description: Validate that every specialist declares exactly one team, and that team exists.
Validate that every team has at least one specialist assigned to it.
Validate that every team owner is a role, and that role has at least one specialist.
Validate that every contract producer and consumer exist in the specialists map.
Validate that no specialist names collide across teams.
